releases.name: LinBox Bionic Box64 v0.4.4 (aarch64)
releases.body:
LinBox bionic rootfs 专用 Box64（aarch64 / NDK bionic 链接 / -DANDROID=ON / ARM_DYNAREC）

- bionic ELF（PT_INTERP=/system/bin/linker64），与 rootfs 内
  wine / mesa / pulseaudio 等二进制同链同形态；box64 本体零
  glibc 依赖
- 完整安装集（不再只有单个 box64 执行文件）：
  `usr/local/bin/box64` + `usr/bin/box64` PATH 入口链接
  + `usr/lib/box64-x86_64-linux-gnu/libc++_shared.so`
  （上游 ANDROID 模式配套，被仿真 x86_64 程序的 C++ 标准库）
  + `usr/etc/box64.box64rc`（系统级调优开关）
  + `usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/`（`ld-linux-aarch64.so.1`
  私有加载器与 aarch64 glibc 运行库 —— glibc 形态 box64
  与 rootfs 内 glibc 二进制的运行层）
  + `usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/`（被仿真 x86_64 程序的
  glibc 运行库，box64 经 BOX64_LD_LIBRARY_PATH 查找）
- 手动安装: 解包 `linbox-box64-*.tar.gz` 至 /（data/data/com.linbox/...
  自动就位），或 `linbox-container install-box64 <tar.gz|URL>`
- 安装后 linbox-container 自动探测 /usr/local/bin/box64
- 用途: 在 aarch64 设备上运行 x86_64 Wine（backend=box64）；
  v0.4.4 为 hangover-11.16 官方配套版本（错配可致 wineboot SEH 级联崩溃）
- 注意: 与完整 rootfs 包（build-bionic-rootfs）同源 —— rootfs 已内置
  同款 box64 与配套文件，单独升级时才需要本包

ares v148 has now been released.

This release includes big improvements to a number of ares cores. Highlights include rewrites to the N64 CPU & RSP JITs resulting in significant performance gains across the N64 library, additional implementation & accuracy improvements to the PlayStation core, fixes to the GBA core, and support for the Famicom data recorder & Dendy.

Since v147, 20 contributors have created 300 commits to the ares codebase.

As always, if you wish to see the full changelog in a per-commit format along with their authors, you can do so on GitHub [here](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/compare/v147...v148).

- **View Settings (Wayland output):** **Scale** had no effect and **Resolution** vs **Scale** did not behave distinctly (only changing resolution drove UI size).

- **Android 10 (API 29) crash fix:** Guarded `InsetsController` behind API >= 30 with safe legacy immersive fallback.
- **Physical stick diagonals & cubemaps:** 2D radial deadzone for full 100% diagonal reach and `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_CUBE_COMPATIBLE_BIT` on square `6n`-layer `2D_ARRAY` images.

## 1.2.2 (2026-11)

### New
- Audio: HRTF filtering (3D sound) can be turned off, globally or per game
  (#374). It's the console's filter for the sounds a game places around you;
  on by default, as before.

  (#367). Before, xbased ran the attacher, which can't load here.
- Time played leaves out the time a game is paused: the pause key, the
  in-game menu, its window minimized (#379).

### Fixes
- Frame rate: a game no longer runs too fast for a moment after a stutter,
  and its frame rate no longer drops when the PC is busy. The emulated
  console's vblank, its clock, could fall behind on a loaded PC or a laptop
  saving power, then caught up in a burst (#370). Its thread now runs at a
  high priority, it never catches up in a burst, and xbased stays out of
  Windows' power throttling, which on laptops moves programs to the slower
  cores and delays their timers.
- Frame rate limits that are a whole number of the display's refreshes (Up
  to 30 or 60 on a 60 Hz display, Unlocked at the display's refresh rate)

releases.body:
## xbased 1.2.0

This is the update I talked about in #353. Thanks to everyone who gave their
opinion there, and to everyone who keeps reporting issues.

### Why this update

1.1.0 replaced xbased's GPU layer with a new one built around the graphics
chip test program [nxdk_pgraph_tests](https://github.com/abaire/nxdk_pgraph_tests).
It matched the console in thousands of those tests, but in games it cost
performance, most of all on Intel GPUs and some AMD GPUs, and it brought
graphical glitches of its own. The Fast precision mode from 1.1.2 helped,
but it was never a full return to 1.0.104, and I haven't found a single
game where the extra precision was worth what it cost.

So 1.2.0 starts again from the GPU layer of 1.0.94, the last version before
that work began. Every game fix and improvement made since then has been
brought over to it. What's left out are the changes that were only there to
match the test program. Everything outside the GPU layer (kernel, CPU,
audio, input and interface) is the same as in 1.1.15, plus this version's
own fixes. From now on the graphics work goes into the glitches that show
up in games.

### What this means for you

releases.body:
**省流：** 不选胶卷也能只用滤镜保存图片，自定义组合保存得更完整；RAW 少占一些内存，测光和曲线少做重复计算。界面保持原样，未大规模真机验证，需要社区反馈。

内部安装版本码递增为 **126**，沿用原发布签名，可覆盖安装。本轮共创：**GPT（OpenAI，AI 助手）**。

### 滤镜和胶卷自由搭配

- 胶卷选“无”后，数字调色和 LUT 继续生效，可通过原有保存入口导出图片。胶卷、相纸和数字调整按用户现有选择组合，不增加模式或范围控件。
- “存为风格”和“分享当前风格”记录当前完整选择，包括明确的无胶卷状态、物理细调、效果开关及记住的强度；重新套用时不再漏掉这些设置。局部蒙版留在当前照片，RAW 白平衡、裁切和边框不进入可复用风格。
- 新版 `.spklook` 写出 version 2，并继续读取旧 version 1 文件。旧应用不能保证还原 v2 的全部新语义；自定义配方基于已有胶卷、相纸及参数，每张图仍使用一个物理方案和一个数字调色层 / LUT。

### RAW 少复制，计算少重复

- 对满足条件的整数 RAW，将解码结果直接转换到工作尺寸，避免先创建完整的浮点中间图；最终 Bitmap 分配前释放已用完的原始存储。
- 对严格兼容的整数 LinearRaw 子集，一次性处理直接接管已有像素存储，减少一份整图复制。浮点精度路径、黑白点及方向处理保留原有约定，并检查取消和失败时的存储状态。
- 同一次显示计算只准备一次曲线；自动测光和场景亮度统计复用已完成的精确分区，减少重复选择工作。逐项对照保留原有数值结果，没有更换胶片光谱、默认显影或成像公式。
- 吸收上游 Sony Huffman 解码缓存索引保护，保留合法索引的既有计算；尚未用真实问题 Sony 原片完成复现验收。

### 验证范围

本轮分项云端验证包含 172 项 Release JVM 测试、3 项原有界面风格保存 / 导入测试、完整 LibRaw 的 ASan / UBSan 检查、ARM64 JNI 编译，以及测光和场景统计的 1460 项数值对照；真实 Vulkan 胶片与印放对照输出保持一致。发布仍须通过整包构建、原生回归、签名证书及 16 KiB 对齐检查。

**未大规模真机验证，需要社区反馈。** 云端的耗时及内存改善不等于手机整张导出同比提速，也不保证所有 RAW 都降低峰值。新 RAW 仍默认线性显示，递归模糊、交互色表及完整外存分块实验继续默认关闭。

**省流：** 修复异常像素被当成正常照片保存，出错后重建引擎重算。未大规模真机验证，需要社区反馈。

这次集中处理社区 [#17](https://github.com/Dear-Ded/Spektralab-X/issues/17) 反馈的窄条画面、黑块和紫色色块。暗房里算坏的底片，不能盖个“保存成功”就交卷。

内部安装版本码递增为 **125**，沿用原发布签名，可覆盖安装。本轮共创：**GPT（OpenAI，AI 助手）**。

### 修复异常像素被放行

- 修复浮点 RGB 中的 NaN、正负无穷在转成整数时丢失错误信息的问题。这些值原来会变成黑色或偏色像素，alpha 和文件结构却仍然正常；只要局部还有画面，旧的纯色检查就可能放行。
- 现在在整数转换和结果缓存前扫描全部 RGB 通道，记录首个异常像素的位置和通道；同时检查扫描工作组是否完整执行。异常结果停止交付，不进入后续保存。
- 导出前还会核对 RGBA16 布局及每个有效像素的 alpha，拦截未完整写入的结果。普通 Bitmap 导出、胶片 JPEG 4:4:4 和 RGBA16 TIFF 共用这项检查。

### 出错后重新开一间暗房

**Fixes**

## Endemic life is visible

Small creatures in the field (Stinkmink, Clothfly and the rest of the endemic life) were invisible in the port: you could still pick them up and get their buffs, but nothing was drawn. The game decides whether to draw them from a visibility test it runs on the GPU and then reads back on the CPU; the port never copied that result back, so the game always read "not visible". Now it does. Only that small result is copied, so the frame rate stays at a locked 30 fps.

- An empty file `sin_devolver_copias` in the game folder brings back the old behaviour.

Thanks to the player who reported it in issue #8.

Nothing else changes: shader caches are the same as in 1.6.0, so your existing caches keep working.

releases.name: MH Rise port v1.5.0
releases.body:
## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 — Release Notes

**2026-11-14 · Windows x64 · Linux x86_64 · macOS Intel**

Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 is a performance release. Nothing in the emulation model changed: every
game still renders the same picture it did in v0.9.9.6, and the same save states still load. What
changed is how much work the CPU and the GPU have to do to get there.

The headline is that the hybrid JIT now translates **more than 80 % of the guest instruction
stream to native x86-64**, the Vulkan renderer stopped paying for a redundant depth write that was
silently disabling hardware Early-Z / Hi-Z culling, and UMA GPUs finally get zero-copy geometry
upload. Together those turn the integrated-GPU experience from "lock it to 496×384" into a picture
that can actually be played at native resolution.

releases.name: v2.5.0
releases.body:
## Highlights

- **Disk images are kept unmodified with a save directory.** With `-saveDir`, what the software writes goes to an overlay file there and the image is only read. Overlays store only the tracks or blocks written and are tied to a checksum of their image. This also makes writable the disks that could not be written before: inside a zip or gzip, loaded from a URL, or embedded in the executable.
- **DOS 3.3 boots in five seconds.** The Disk II motor keeps turning for about a second after the drive is turned off, like the 556 timer of the real controller, and the data latch no longer reads the same nibble twice. DOS no longer waits for the motor on every access: a DOS 3.3 boot takes 5.4 million cycles instead of 36 million.
- **A libretro core** runs izapple2 inside RetroArch and the other libretro frontends, with diskette swapping from M3U playlists and saves as overlays. It is built from source and is not in the release archives. See [the libretro page](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro.md) and [the Mac guide](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro_macos.md).

releases.body:
**Headlight beams in both games, and the first Android beta.** At night your car finally lights up the road ahead and we're releasing the Android version for further testing.

## Features

- **Headlight beams.** Turning your lights on at night now throws a beam of light onto the road ahead, as on the original Xbox: it brightens the street, cars and walls it reaches and stops where it meets them ([#10](https://github.com/laureladastra/mcdub3-nx/issues/10), thanks for the report). Before, the lights worked in the game but no beam was drawn. Other emulators (i.e. xemu → https://github.com/xemu-project/xemu/issues/996) show a solid white shape instead. The game builds the beam in a small hidden picture using two tricks of the Xbox's graphics chip that the port did not reproduce yet: it reuses a picture as a depth map, and it counts the beam's layers with a special blending mode that works with negative numbers. Both are emulated now. Tested in the DUB Edition and the Remix. The WHITE button flashes your high beams while you hold it. The main headlights are on by themselves at night.

releases.name: mcdub3-nx v1.0.0
releases.body:
**Version 1.0 for both games on the Nintendo Switch.** This release removes the last annoyances: races that felt slow when the frame rate dipped, random zoom-in or out during loading screens, and vertical lines during upscaling.

### Features

- **Races keep their real speed.** The original game moves the race forward by a fixed step every frame, which was fine on the Xbox, where it runs on a fixed 30 FPS. On the Switch, in rain, with nitrous or in the busiest streets, the frame rate can dip and the whole race then went into slow motion. The race now proceeds by the time that really passed. Racing in the rain and with nitrous feels much steadier.
- **No more random zooms during loading screens.** Menus and loading screens are drawn for 4:3 TVs, with black strips at the sides, and the port enlarges them to fill your 16:9 screen. When something briefly reached those strips (the circle animation on loading screens for example), the picture behind it jumped in size for a brief moment. The size stays put now.

releases.name: mcdub3-nx v0.5.0
releases.body:
**A big speed update for both games on the Switch.** Races, especially in the rain, now run close to the game's own top speed of 30 FPS most of the time. Freezes during races are minimised.

### Features

- Measured in rain races on the Switch (at the default 1x picture size):

  |                                    | v0.4.0                 | v0.5.0   |
  | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------- | -------- |
  | Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition       | 23 frames per second   | **28.5** |
  | Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition Remix | 20.5 frames per second | **27.5** |

  The game itself never runs faster than 30, as on the original Xbox, so most of the time you are now at or near full speed.
- **No more half-second freezes in races.** The game stopped for about half a second now and then during a race, most often right after the start.
- **Sharper look for less effort (Remix).** The Remix's glow and blur effects are drawn at normal size even when you raise the picture size, which cost a lot of speed for something that is blurred anyway.

### Other changes

- Each game now has its own tuned graphics settings, so improving one game does not change the other.

releases.name: mcdub3-nx v0.4.0
releases.body:
**This is the first release of Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition Remix**. Runs from boot to the finish line: intro movies, menus, garage, career and races, with music and sound. It ships next to the DUB Edition as its own app, `mcdub3remix-nx-eur.nro`.

### Features

- **Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition Remix.** A new app for this game: `mcdub3remix-nx-eur.nro` on the Switch (in `sdmc:/switch/mcdub3remix-nx/`, disc in `game-eur/` or `game/`), and a Mac app built with `make mac-app GAME=remix`.
- **Remix races play as they should.** From the countdown on, the camera no longer turns into a spinning top view, you can drive, and the pause and options menus appear centred with their list shown once.
- **More of the game converted correctly.** Floating-point comparisons now give the same answers as the Xbox's processor, also when a value is not a number. The Remix's code relies on this throughout (it was compiled for the Xbox's SSE unit, the DUB Edition mostly for the older x87 one).

releases.name: mcdub3-nx v0.3.0
releases.body:

- **Smooth loading screens.** The circles on the career loading screen now turn smoothly and close, on every platform. The game copies each frame into the next one with the Xbox GPU's 2D engine and only draws what changed.

A stability and hygiene patch for v2.0.0, focused on the crash and antivirus reports from the first few hours.

- Windows: `Skate3Recomp-Windows.zip`
- Linux: `Skate3Recomp-Linux.zip`
- macOS: `Skate3Recomp-macOS.zip`

## Changes

#### Stability

- Fixed a crash on Linux and macOS where the game could die suddenly during gameplay when world streaming revoked memory the renderer was reading
- Fixed distant demoted tree trunks rendering with a flat blue texture

#### Antivirus false positives

- The Windows executable and runtime DLL now carry proper version metadata, and the runtime no longer contains any ability to create executable memory (it never used it - all game code is compiled at build time); both changes target the machine-learning heuristics some antivirus engines were tripping on

releases.body:
What's new in 0.78

For players
- **32-bit devices:** one APK now holds both ARMv8 (arm64-v8a) and ARMv7
  (armeabi-v7a). Android picks the right one on install, so 64-bit devices
  always run the 64-bit version. OpenGL ES 3.0 is still required.
- **Screen orientation:** the setting now applies to the launcher as well as
  the game and takes effect at once. Auto respects the system rotation lock.
- **Sound:** the audio buffer margin now adapts to the device.
- **Launcher:** new Advanced screen with a Debug mode switch. With it off,
  nothing is written to the log.
- **Logs:** new screen under Data to export, share or send logs to the
  developer, or clear them.

Under the hood
- **Most of the game is now ported C++:** - game code is moving from recompiled to ported native ARM code.
- **Old processor code removed:** x87 emulation is gone from the generated
  code, and the whole game runs in 24-bit floating point. MMX, CPU detection
  and the Pentium FDIV workarounds are removed too.

Known limits
- ARMv7 has only been tested in the 32-bit mode of a 64-bit phone, not on a
  real 32-bit device, so speed on older hardware is unknown.

releases.name: v0.4.7
releases.body:
Phones get new defaults that run smoother and cooler, voices on Android should come through again, and every platform gets a Render scale option. Everything from [0.4.6](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.6) is included.

## Android

- **Frame rate unlocked with a 45 fps limit, by default.** Uncapped, the phone's GPU runs at full load until the phone lowers its clock as it heats up; the limit keeps headroom. The limit drops to the nearest rate that divides your screen's refresh, so every frame lasts the same: 40 fps on a 120 Hz screen (Galaxy S24/S25), 45 at 90 Hz, 30 at 60 Hz. On an S25 Ultra frame times went from a 25/25/16.7 ms mix to an even 25 ms. You can still pick 30, 60 or no limit in Device Options > Display > Frame rate limit.
- **Render scale 75 % by default.** The 3D scene is drawn at 75 % and scaled up to the screen; on an S25 Ultra that is 14 % less GPU work per frame, with a slightly softer picture. Graphics > Render scale goes back to 100 %.
- **Snapdragon GSR for the final upscale by default**, one pass instead of FSR 1's two.

releases.name: v0.4.6
releases.body:
Insane can now be picked from the start. Everything from [0.4.5](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.5) is included; if you have not read its notes, they cover the Riftworm fix for Vulkan, GPU detection on Linux and Proton, and the co-op go-to-player-1 key.

## Every platform

- **Insane without finishing the campaign first.** The option from 0.4.5, now named **All chapters and Insane unlocked** (PC Options > Saves, on by default), also enables the Insane button in the difficulty menu, in solo Campaign and in the co-op lobby. Before, the game greyed it out until the campaign had been finished once. As with chapters, only the menu check changes: your saved progress and the Extras list of unlockables are not touched.

## Known, still open

- Lighting that looks pixelated on Linux with presets above Low, and black textures on Low on Windows (both on a Legion Go): we could not reproduce them on our PC. A screenshot and the `logs/gow2_*.log` of the run, with the chapter, help a lot.

releases.name: v0.4.5
releases.body:
The Riftworm interior no longer crashes or goes black with Vulkan, the game picks the right GPU settings on Linux and under Proton, every chapter can be picked from the start, and co-op gets a key and a controller combo to go to player 1. Everything from [0.4.4](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.4) is included.

## Vulkan (Linux and SteamOS, Proton with Vulkan, Android, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Inside the Riftworm (act 5) no longer loses the GPU.** The worm's flesh is drawn with tessellation, and the shaders the renderer builds for it read their settings from the wrong slot, so the tessellation factor came from unrelated memory: the scene stayed black, would not load, or the game closed with a lost device. Fixed in SDK patch 0091 (found with the Khronos validation layer). On a Radeon RX 7800 XT the worm interior now runs 120 s at 60 fps where it failed within seconds. Under Proton, Vulkan (`gpu_backend = vulkan`) is the backend to use for that chapter: D3D12 through vkd3d-proton was also reported to lose the device there and we could not test it.

## Linux and SteamOS

releases.name: v0.4.4
releases.body:
Less memory traffic on phone GPUs, less work per draw on the GPU command thread, and a new option for the CPU core the game spins while it waits for the GPU. Everything from [0.4.3](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.3) is included.

## Vulkan (Android, Linux and SteamOS, Vulkan on Windows)

- **Each render pass now covers only what it draws.** The renderer sizes its render targets for the console's whole EDRAM (1520x3456 on the phone) and every render pass loaded and stored all of it, even when its draws touched only the 1280x720 of a 720p frame. Phone GPUs render in tiles and pay for every byte a pass loads and stores, so they moved about 5.7 times the memory they needed. Now each pass begins with only the area its draws and clears can write (SDK patch 0089). It follows the Vulkan rules, so the picture should not change; it has not been measured on a phone yet. If part of the picture looks missing or stale, set `vulkan_tight_render_area = false` in `gow2.toml` (it takes effect at once) and open an issue with the scene. Direct3D 12, the Windows default, is not affected.

## Every platform

releases.name: v0.4.3
releases.body:
A new Android APK that survives leaving the game, a leaner game binary on every platform, and threads that sleep instead of polling on Linux and Android. Everything from [0.4.2](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.2) is included.

## Android

- **Leaving the game and coming back no longer crashes it.** Home, switching to another app or the screen turning off, then coming back: up to 0.3.18 the return crashed (in `vkCreateAndroidSurfaceKHR`, with a window Android had already freed). Now the game lets go of the old window when it leaves the screen and connects to the new one when it comes back (SDK patch 0085). The game keeps running while it is off screen (only the picture and the sound stop), so pause it before you leave.
- **The update dialog holds the game until you answer it**, instead of letting it start behind the dialog, and the phone only offers releases that carry an APK (0.4.2 was for PC and Linux only).

santiquiroz-gears-of-war-2-pc-port.latest_body:
Phones get new defaults that run smoother and cooler, voices on Android should come through again, and every platform gets a Render scale option. Everything from [0.4.6](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/tag/v0.4.6) is included.

## Android

- **Frame rate unlocked with a 45 fps limit, by default.** Uncapped, the phone's GPU runs at full load until the phone lowers its clock as it heats up; the limit keeps headroom. The limit drops to the nearest rate that divides your screen's refresh, so every frame lasts the same: 40 fps on a 120 Hz screen (Galaxy S24/S25), 45 at 90 Hz, 30 at 60 Hz. On an S25 Ultra frame times went from a 25/25/16.7 ms mix to an even 25 ms. You can still pick 30, 60 or no limit in Device Options > Display > Frame rate limit.
- **Render scale 75 % by default.** The 3D scene is drawn at 75 % and scaled up to the screen; on an S25 Ultra that is 14 % less GPU work per frame, with a slightly softer picture. Graphics > Render scale goes back to 100 %.
- **Snapdragon GSR for the final upscale by default**, one pass instead of FSR 1's two.

shadPS4 v0.18.0 "UltraPersona"

Hello there, it hasn't been a while, has it? While not much time has passed since our last stable release, we are here again with a brand new one. The main reason for this release is broken shadNet authorization in certain cases on the 0.17.0 release, but we have some more interesting new features as well.

Firstly, after some fixes, AvPlayer can now be loaded as LLE, meaning that you need the `libSceAvPlayer.sprx` (and `libSceAvPlayerStreaming.sprx`) module(s), which makes broken videos in a few games now work properly.

The above change was enabled by calling `sceLibcInternalMemoryMutexEnable` in LLE LibcInternal at boot, found by [@liuk7071](https://github.com/liuk7071), the developer of ChonkyStation4, another PS4 emulator.

A kernel event flag rewrite has also fixed Shadow of the Colossus often hanging on boot, and the game now consistently gets to menus.

releases.name: NSP Box 4.0.0 — Meet NUP
releases.body:
# NSP Box 4.0.0 — Meet NUP

Smaller archives, flexible packaging, and more control over your game collection. Version 4.0 introduces **NUP Tools**, alongside the existing NSP builder.

### Package more. Store less.

- **Create compressed NUP archives** from extracted game folders, with base games, updates and DLC together in one file.
- **Choose your balance:** Fast for quicker compression, Balanced for everyday use, or Smaller for stronger compression. Incompressible files are stored raw automatically.
- **Keep what you need:** select Base, Updates and DLC independently. Choices appear after inspection, only for content present in your source. Latest-snapshot mode merges the newest selected update with the selected base, retains required base-only files, and leaves superseded versions behind. Turn it off to keep separate base/update records.
- **Avoid duplicate storage:** identical file contents can share the same space inside an archive.
- **Stay compatible:** leave files larger than 256 MiB uncompressed to reduce temporary decompression work in supported emulators.

### Convert, extract and check

- **NSP → NUP:** compress plaintext NSPs created by NSP Box.

releases.name: NSP Box 3.1.0
releases.body:
# NSP Box 3.1.0

- **Selevet support:** the emulator patcher now supports Selevet Eglantine performance build 4, including both normal and 30 FPS Windows downloads.
- **Future-build matching:** minor Selevet updates can be recognized when the reviewed loader and metadata-reader fingerprints still match. Unverified matches are labeled experimental; changed or ambiguous hooks are refused.
- **Settings preserved:** adding or removing the metadata patch keeps `nx2_switches.txt` and the existing 30 FPS setting unchanged. Exact original executable backups remain available for removal.
- **Supported-build list:** added Selevet and adjusted the patch dialog so its full compatibility list remains visible.
- **Validation:** both Selevet downloads passed byte-exact patch removal, isolated native hook checks and real startup timing comparisons. Patched startup without a companion matched the external-NPDM path at 31.25 MHz. These checks do not establish gameplay compatibility or FPS gains.

- **New branding:** NSP Box, with redesigned icons and a new app logo.
- **Smoother UI:** subtle animated background, fluid transitions, and improved spacing.
- **NSP-only packaging:** removed XCI output from games and DLC.
- **Dedicated DLC tab:** create separate DLC NSPs for compatible emulators. Thanks [@ryzendew](https://github.com/ryzendew) for requesting separate packages in [#1](https://github.com/smarkyie/switch2-game-packager/issues/1).

releases.name: Switch 2 Game Packager 2.0.0
releases.body:
# Switch 2 Game Packager 2.0.0

- **New Emulator patch panel:** select a Windows x64 emulator folder, check compatibility, add the patch and remove it later. Eglantine build 96 standard/PGO and PokeDinner 2.0.0 GUI/CLI profiles are recognized; matching future builds and forks can be tried experimentally without a new menu entry.
- **No separate `main.npdm` needed after patching:** compatible emulators read Switch 2 metadata already embedded inside this packager's plaintext XCI/NSP. Restart the emulator after applying the patch. Existing packages do not need rebuilding, and the packager need not remain open while playing.
- To create only a single XCI/NSP, uncheck **Create package folder**. The option remains on by default for unpatched emulators; without the patch, retain each game's exact external companion in its own folder. Selecting 12 GiB alone can still use incorrect timing and reduce performance.

releases.body:
# Skyrim for Android 0.30.6

APK: `Skyrim-0.30.6.apk` (arm64-v8a, Android 9+, Vulkan 1.1).

## New
- "Disable end-of-frame image space (post-processing)" option. It does the same as the TEOFIS console command at every launch. It fixes the black world map and solid-colour underwater screen, but it also turns off all end-of-frame post-processing (tonemapping, bloom, colour grading and depth of field), so the game looks more naturally lit.
- "Asynchronous rendering" option. It's off by default and when it's on, shaders compile on background threads. New effects may pop in for a frame or two instead of causing a hitch. 

## Fixed
- Shader caching is removed. The DXVK state cache rebuilt every saved pipeline on 5 extra threads at startup, which took CPU away from the game's main thread and caused crashes on Mali devices. Nothing is cached between launches now, and the game runs better overall.
- Traps triggering freezes was due to failed lookups with vertex optimization. The function has been turned off for now.
- Audio in other languages - the decoder was reading each WMA bitstream but with the wrong block-size config. Should be working now.

Hotfix release following 0.3.0: fixes a frame-pacing and input-latency regression in input polling, eliminates shader-translation busy-wait CPU spikes, adds a 20 FPS limiter option, and enables full resolve readback automatically for FIFA Street (2012).

* Fix the 0.3.0 `jit_frame_start` polling-hold regression (stuttering / sluggish input in CoD MW2 and other titles) and switch the default back to Off (#144)
* Replace shader-translation busy-spin loops with `std::atomic::wait` and drop an unnecessary audio stub yield to reduce battery draw and frame-time spikes (#123)

### Genma Onimusha — Android ARM64 Port (v0.7.0-android.1)

- **Mode Build CI**: `asset-free-runtime`
- **Target Minimum**: Android 10+ (API 29+), ABI `arm64-v8a`
- **Grafis**: Vulkan 1.0+ Fallback (Adreno/Mali) + SPIR-V pra-kompilasi
- **Folder Data di HP**: `/storage/emulated/0/GenmaOnimusha` (salin `.iso` atau ekstrak `default.xbe` beserta folder game, dan opsional `textures/` untuk HD Texture Pack)
